title: In Art We Trust
authors: Yuexin Li; Xiaoyin Ma; Luc D. R. Renneboog
eligible_reason: Table 3 exploits discoveries of fakes and forgeries at artist-specific dates (forged_artist x post discovery_date; artists and dates in Online Appendix Table A.IV) with artist FE and year and month FE, a staggered binary design in principle. But every column's parameter of interest is treated x provenance (subgroup-by-treatment interaction), all columns include lot-level hedonic covariates, and time FE are year plus month-of-year. Table 4 (Christie's provenance policy change) has one treated auction house and one date. Other tables are hedonic or repeat-sales regressions. Not a near-miss: the binding violation is the subgroup-by-treatment interaction, not time-varying controls.
design_notes: Stata MS_LiMaRenneboog.do. Hedonic sample of auction lots (Blouin Art Sales Index; N = 1,111,220 in Table 3 col 1 per log). Table 3: reghdfe lnprice treated provenance treated_provenance $basic_hedonic i.year i.month, absorb(aid) vce(cluster AH_id). Appendix C repeats with sold as outcome (ln_reserve_price added).
n_adoption_cohorts_note: Number of forged artists/discovery dates is in Online Appendix Table A.IV (not available); the 100-row sample file has forged_artist = 0 throughout.
